messages.content: Predict this human participant’s actual choice in a repeated two-person game. The same randomly matched real partner stays throughout the interaction. In each round, both people privately click Split (cooperate) or Steal (defect). Choices are made without seeing the other person’s current choice, then both choices and the outcome are shown once both have submitted. Payoffs are lottery tickets: if both choose Split, each receives 5; if you choose Split and the other chooses Steal, you receive 0 and the other receives 10; if you choose Steal and the other chooses Split, you receive 10 and the other receives 0; if both choose Steal, each receives 1. Tickets accumulate; the screen displays both people’s ticket totals. Each ticket enters a monetary prize draw with one £100 prize and two £50 prizes; more tickets increase the chance of winning. There is also a fixed £10 participation payment. Tickets have no stated fixed cash conversion. The two people sit in separate cubicles and see live video of their own and their partner’s faces. Audio is disabled; they must not talk or use hand gestures, but may use facial expressions. Return only Split or Steal.
